subject.title: fix(codex): ungate app-server terminal liveness and fan out poisoned-client retirement

question: Should Codex terminal-idle be a hard physical-client liveness cap even while OpenClaw is awaiting app-server server-request responses, and should timed-out turns immediately close co-leased shared clients?
rationale: The code fix matches the linked liveness bug, but it intentionally changes behavior for existing long silent request waits and co-leased sessions; automation cannot choose that product/compatibility tradeoff safely.

options.title: Accept the hard liveness cap
options.body: Proceed with this PR's scoped behavior and document that a suspect shared Codex client can abort co-leased turns and that silent in-flight requests are bounded by terminal idle.

options.title: Preserve long pending waits
options.body: Revise the PR to exempt or separately time known human-wait request types such as user input before removing the request gate globally.

options.title: Pause for the lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this branch under the broader run-lifecycle design if maintainers want one unified liveness owner before changing Codex app-server behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the hard liveness cap
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR's scoped behavior and document that a suspect shared Codex client can abort co-leased turns and that silent in-flight requests are bounded by terminal idle.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server routing and lifecycle refactors make steipete the best available owner for this compatibility tradeoff.
